claim: Influencer marketing returns $5.78 for every $1 spent
commonly_cited_as: "Influencer marketing ROI is $5.78 per $1" (as revenue or ROI)
origin_title: The State of Influencer Marketing 2020: Benchmark Report
quote: Average earned media value per $1 spent has increased to $5.78
safe_rephrasing: Respondents to Influencer Marketing Hub's 2020 survey reported an average $5.78 in earned media value — not sales — per $1 spent in 2019.

claim: Businesses make $6.50 for every $1 spent on influencer marketing
commonly_cited_as: "Influencer marketing delivers $6.50 ROI" (as a current benchmark)
origin_title: Influencer Marketing Study (blog post)
quote: Tomoson surveyed 125 marketers online from 10–16 March 2015.
safe_rephrasing: In a 2015 poll of 125 marketers by influencer platform Tomoson, respondents self-reported an average $6.50 return per $1.

claim: Email marketing returns $36 for every $1 spent
commonly_cited_as: "Email ROI is 36:1" (as measured and current)
origin_title: State of Email Survey 2020
quote: These insights are derived from Litmus’ 2020 State of Email Survey of more than 2,000 marketing professionals worldwide.
safe_rephrasing: Marketers surveyed by Litmus in 2020 self-reported an average email ROI of about 36:1; in 2025, 35% of marketing leaders reported $10–36 per $1.

claim: 92% of consumers trust influencers, UGC or word of mouth more than ads
commonly_cited_as: "92% of consumers trust influencers (or UGC) over ads" — Nielsen
origin_title: Global Trust in Advertising (April 2012)
quote: “recommendations from people I know” scored highest on trust, with 92 percent of consumers trusting this source completely or somewhat.
safe_rephrasing: In Nielsen's 2012 global online survey, 92% said they trust recommendations from people they know completely or somewhat; ads on social networks were trusted by 36%.

claim: 61% of consumers trust influencer recommendations vs 38% for brands
commonly_cited_as: "61% trust influencers, only 38% trust brands"
origin_title: Matter Survey Reveals Consumers Find Influencers More Helpful and Trustworthy than Brands During the Pandemic
quote: 61% are likely to trust recommendations from a friend, family member or influencer on social platforms.
safe_rephrasing: A May 2020 Matter Communications survey of 1,000 US adults found 61% likely to trust recommendations from friends, family or influencers on social, versus 38% from brands.

claim: The average person sees 4,000–10,000 ads a day
commonly_cited_as: "We see up to 10,000 ads a day"
origin_publisher: None — traced to a 2006 CBS interview quote
origin_title: No study; disowned by the person credited
quote: "Our intention was not to endorse any particular number" — J. Walker Smith to The Drum. The 4A's (2007): "These numbers are unsubstantiated."
safe_rephrasing: Estimates of daily ad exposure vary widely; counted studies found roughly 76–362 exposures a day, far fewer of them noticed.

claim: Human attention span is 8 seconds, shorter than a goldfish's 9
commonly_cited_as: "Microsoft study: attention spans shorter than a goldfish"
origin_publisher: None — Microsoft Canada (2015) cited the website Statistic Brain
origin_title: No traceable data
quote: the figure that everyone picked up on … did not actually come from Microsoft's research.
safe_rephrasing: There is no measured 'average attention span'; attention depends on the task and the content (BBC More or Less, 2017).

claim: Prospects need 7 touches before they buy (the Rule of 7)
commonly_cited_as: "1930s Hollywood studios found 7 exposures are needed"
origin_publisher: Jeffrey Lant (book, 1990) — rule of thumb, not a study
origin_title: No study found for the Hollywood story
quote: We searched for the Hollywood 'seven posters' research and couldn't find a single source that names the studio, the year or the study.
safe_rephrasing: The 'Rule of 7' is a rule of thumb; advertising research on effective frequency has proposed 2–3 exposures, and results vary by brand and channel.

claim: Viewers retain 95% of a message in video vs 10% in text
commonly_cited_as: "Studies show viewers retain 95% of a video message"
origin_title: Why Do Viewers Retain 95% of a Video Message, But Only 10% of Text?
quote: It was directional. It was not a peer-reviewed neuroscience study.
safe_rephrasing: Don't cite 95%/10%. If needed, say video can improve recall for complex topics, and cite peer-reviewed work on dual coding.

claim: A 5% increase in customer retention increases profits by 25–95%
commonly_cited_as: "Bain: +5% retention = +25–95% profit" (any business)
origin_title: E-Loyalty: Your Secret Weapon on the Web
quote: By retaining a mere 5% more customers, e-companies can boost profits by 25–95%
safe_rephrasing: Bain's Reichheld estimated in 2000 that retaining 5% more customers could lift e-commerce profits by 25–95%; his 1990 HBR cases (bank, insurance, auto service) showed 25–85% gains in customer value. The effect varies by industry, so model it with your own retention and margin data.

claim: Acquiring a new customer costs 5–25x more than retaining one
commonly_cited_as: "HBR: acquisition costs 5–25x more than retention"
origin_publisher: None — HBR (2014) cites no specific study
origin_title: The Value of Keeping the Right Customers (HBR, Amy Gallo)
quote: Depending on which study you believe, and what industry you’re in, acquiring a new customer is anywhere from five to 25 times more expensive
safe_rephrasing: Acquisition is often more expensive than retention, but the ratio depends on the industry; measure your own CAC against retention cost.

claim: Content marketing costs 62% less than traditional marketing and generates 3x as many leads
commonly_cited_as: "Demand Metric study"
origin_title: Infographic: Content Marketing
quote: This infographic provides statistics and best practices for content marketing.
safe_rephrasing: Don't cite it. Use a current survey with a stated method (e.g. CMI/MarketingProfs annual B2B research) and name its sample.

claim: Businesses make $2 (or $8) for every $1 spent on Google Ads
commonly_cited_as: "Google Ads returns $2 / $8 per $1" (as measured ROI)
origin_title: How we calculate Google’s economic impact
quote: we assume that for every $1 businesses spend on Google Ads, they generate an average of $2 in profit.
safe_rephrasing: Google's economic-impact model assumes $2 in profit per $1 of Google Ads, and $8 when organic search clicks are included.

claim: B2B buyers are 57% through the purchase decision before talking to sales
commonly_cited_as: "Buyers are 57% (or 70%) done before contacting a vendor" (as current)
origin_title: The Digital Evolution in B2B Marketing
quote: the average customer had completed 57% of the purchase decision-making process prior to engaging a supplier sales rep directly.
safe_rephrasing: CEB research from 2012 found B2B buyers were on average 57% through the purchase process before engaging a sales rep.

claim: US creator economy ad spend reaches $37B in 2025
commonly_cited_as: "Creator ad spend hits $37B, growing 4x faster than media"
origin_title: 2025 Creator Economy Ad Spend & Strategy Report
quote: creator economy ad spend is projected to reach $37 billion in 2025 — a 26% increase year-over-year
safe_rephrasing: IAB projected US brands would spend $37B on creator advertising in 2025, up 26% year over year.

claim: Color increases brand recognition by 80%
commonly_cited_as: "University of Loyola study: color increases brand recognition by up to 80%"
origin_publisher: Xerox marketing leaflet (2001/2005), attributed to Loyola University Maryland researchers
origin_title: No study containing the figure was found
quote: Google couldn't find any paper by dr. Hoadley that had that quote in it.
safe_rephrasing: Don't cite a number. If you need evidence on color, cite a named peer-reviewed study and what it measured.

claim: Every 100ms of latency cost Amazon 1% of sales
commonly_cited_as: "Amazon found every 100ms of latency costs 1% in sales"
origin_publisher: Greg Linden (ex-Amazon) blog post and slides, 2006, about a pre-2002 A/B test
origin_title: No published data
quote: In A/B tests, we tried delaying the page in increments of 100 milliseconds and found that even very small delays would result in substantial and costly drops in revenue.
safe_rephrasing: An early-2000s internal Amazon A/B test reportedly found small page delays reduced revenue; no data was published.

claim: Users form an opinion about your website in 50 milliseconds (0.05 s)
commonly_cited_as: "You have 0.05 seconds to make a good first impression"
origin_title: Attention web designers: You have 50 milliseconds to make a good first impression! (Behaviour & Information Technology 25(2))
quote: Study 3 again replicated the 500 ms condition as well as adding a 50 ms condition using the same stimuli
safe_rephrasing: A 2006 lab study found people's ratings of a homepage's visual appeal after 50 ms were consistent with ratings after longer exposure.

claim: 88% of consumers trust online reviews as much as personal recommendations
commonly_cited_as: "88% of consumers trust online reviews as much as personal recommendations" (as current)
origin_title: Local Consumer Review Survey 2014
quote: 88% of consumers say they trust online reviews as much as personal recommendations (vs. 79% in 2013)
safe_rephrasing: In BrightLocal's 2014 panel survey, 88% said they trust online reviews as much as personal recommendations; the same company's recent editions report around half.

claim: People are 4x more likely to buy when referred by a friend (Nielsen)
commonly_cited_as: "Customers are 4x more likely to buy when referred by a friend" — Nielsen
origin_publisher: None. The Nielsen release usually cited does not contain it
origin_title: Nielsen Global Online Consumer Survey press release (July 2009)
quote: nine in every ten Internet consumers worldwide (90 percent) trust recommendations from people they know
safe_rephrasing: Don't cite '4x'. Nielsen's 2009 global survey found 90% trust recommendations from people they know.

claim: Personalized emails deliver 6x higher transaction rates
commonly_cited_as: "Personalized emails deliver 6x higher transaction rates" (as current)
origin_title: 2013 Email Market Study (press release, 5 Feb 2014)
quote: The study found that personalized emails generate six times higher transaction rates and revenue per email than nonpersonalized email.
safe_rephrasing: Experian's 2013 analysis of its clients' emails found personalized emails had six times the transaction rate of non-personalized ones.

claim: Word of mouth drives 13% of consumer sales ($6 trillion)
commonly_cited_as: "Word of mouth drives $6 trillion of annual consumer spending"
origin_publisher: Word of Mouth Marketing Association (WOMMA), analysis by Analytic Partners
origin_title: Return on Word of Mouth (press release, 18 Nov 2014)
quote: online and offline consumer conversations and recommendations account for 13% of consumer sales, on average, which represents $6 trillion in annual consumer spending.
safe_rephrasing: A 2014 WOMMA-sponsored model of six categories estimated word of mouth drove about 13% of sales for participating brands.

claim: Consumers are 71% more likely to purchase based on social media referrals
commonly_cited_as: "HubSpot: 71% more likely to purchase based on social media referrals"
origin_title: 71% More Likely to Purchase Based on Social Media Referrals [Infographic]
quote: No quote available: the original HubSpot URL now redirects to an unrelated article.
safe_rephrasing: Don't cite it; use a current survey with a stated sample.

claim: Millennials trust user-generated content 50% more than other media
commonly_cited_as: "Millennials trust UGC 50% more than traditional media" (as current)
origin_title: Social Influence: Marketing's New Frontier (as reported by Adweek)
quote: A study by Crowdtap and Ipsos Media CT found that this generation is most influenced by user-generated content (UGC).
safe_rephrasing: A 2014 survey by UGC firm Crowdtap with Ipsos found millennials rated user-generated content as more trusted than other media.

claim: The brain processes visuals 60,000 times faster than text
commonly_cited_as: "3M research: visuals are processed 60,000x faster than text"
origin_title: No study found
quote: the 2001 3M document you get is not a research summary, not product of their R&D, but a sales brochure
safe_rephrasing: Don't cite it. Images can be understood quickly, but no study supports '60,000 times'.

claim: 80% of sales require 5 follow-ups
commonly_cited_as: "80% of sales require 5 follow-up calls" (National Sales Executive Association)
origin_publisher: Long Island chapter of the National Sales Executives Association (now SMEI)
origin_title: Member survey
quote: 80% of sales are made on the fifth to twelfth contact
safe_rephrasing: A 1942 survey of fewer than 40 sales executives reported most sales closing after several contacts; it is not modern evidence.

claim: Text messages have a 98% open rate
commonly_cited_as: "SMS has a 98% open rate (vs 20% for email)"
origin_title: Conversational Advertising (white paper)
quote: neither datapoints represent an accurate reflection of today's world of mobile messaging.
safe_rephrasing: Mobilesquared's 2010 estimate of 98% SMS read rates is withdrawn by its author; its 2022 data suggests about 55% are read.

claim: Only 7% of communication is words (7-38-55 rule)
commonly_cited_as: "93% of communication is nonverbal"
origin_title: Mehrabian & Wiener 1967; Mehrabian & Ferris 1967; Silent Messages (1971/1981)
quote: was actually concerned with feelings and attitudes
safe_rephrasing: Mehrabian's 1960s experiments concern how people judge feelings when words and tone conflict; he says the ratios don't apply to communication in general.

claim: 75% of users never scroll past the first page of search results
commonly_cited_as: "75% of users never scroll past the first page of Google" — HubSpot
origin_title: 120 Awesome Marketing Stats, Charts and Graphs
quote: That underlying source is a dead link.
safe_rephrasing: Don't cite 75%. Use a dated click-through study and name its data source.

claim: 53% of mobile users abandon a site that takes over 3 seconds to load
commonly_cited_as: "53% of mobile visitors leave if a page takes longer than 3 seconds" (as current)
origin_title: The need for mobile speed
quote: 53% of visits are likely to be abandoned if pages take longer than 3 seconds to load
safe_rephrasing: Google's 2016 analysis of ~3,700 mobile sites estimated 53% of visits are likely abandoned when pages take over 3 seconds.

claim: 89% of companies compete primarily on customer experience (Gartner)
commonly_cited_as: "89% of businesses compete primarily on customer experience"
origin_title: Customer experience survey (2014)
quote: 89% of companies expect to compete primarily on the basis of customer experience
safe_rephrasing: In a 2014 Gartner survey, 89% of companies said they expected to compete mainly on customer experience.

claim: 49% of consumers depend on influencer recommendations
commonly_cited_as: "49% of consumers rely on influencer recommendations" (as US consumers today)
origin_title: Twitter influencer study (2016)
quote: Almost half of the respondents (49 percent) in the survey rely on influencers for product recommen[dations]
safe_rephrasing: In a 2016 Twitter/Annalect survey of Twitter users, 49% said they rely on influencers for product recommendations.

claim: 70% of teens trust YouTubers more than traditional celebrities
commonly_cited_as: "70% of teenagers trust influencers more than celebrities"
origin_title: The YouTube Generation Study (Think with Google)
quote: teen YouTube channel subscribers who agreed that YouTube creators are “more like one of us” than traditional celebrities, n=433, Nov. 2015.
safe_rephrasing: In a 2015 Google-commissioned survey of 433 US teen YouTube subscribers, 70% said they relate to YouTube creators more than to traditional celebrities.

claim: 80% of consumers are more likely to buy when brands offer personalized experiences
commonly_cited_as: "80% of consumers are more likely to buy from brands that personalize" (as current)
origin_title: The power of me: The impact of personalization on marketing performance (press release, 9 Jan 2018)
quote: 80% of respondents indicating they are more likely to do business with a com[pany if it offers personalized experiences]
safe_rephrasing: In Epsilon's 2017 survey of 1,000 US consumers, 80% said they're more likely to do business with a company offering personalized experiences.

claim: People remember 10% of what they read, 20% of what they hear…
commonly_cited_as: "Dale's Cone: we remember 10% of what we read, 90% of what we do"
origin_publisher: D. G. Treichler (Mobil Oil employee), Film and Audio-Visual Communications magazine
origin_title: No research cited
quote: D. G. Treichler didn't cite any research
safe_rephrasing: Don't cite these percentages; Dale's cone has no numbers and no research supports them.

claim: Inbound leads cost 61% less than outbound leads
commonly_cited_as: "Inbound leads cost 61% less than outbound" (as current)
origin_title: State of Inbound Marketing (2012; earlier editions 2009-2011)
quote: the 2009 survey showed that inbound marketing dominated organizations experienced a 61% lower cost per lead
safe_rephrasing: HubSpot's 2009-2012 surveys of marketers reported roughly 60% lower cost per lead for inbound-dominated companies.

claim: Companies that blog get 55% more website visitors
commonly_cited_as: "Companies that blog get 55% more visitors, 97% more links, 434% more indexed pages"
origin_title: Analysis of HubSpot customers' websites (reported Aug 2009)
quote: that's the average increase in visitors to small business websites as a result of blogging, according to the study.
safe_rephrasing: A 2009 HubSpot comparison of its small-business customers found those with blogs averaged 55% more visitors.

claim: Video on a landing page increases conversions by 80%
commonly_cited_as: "Adding video to a landing page increases conversion by 80%"
origin_publisher: Attributed to an EyeView case study; no data published
origin_title: No study found
quote: Videos do not boost your landing page conversion rates—and in some cases, might even harm them.
safe_rephrasing: Don't cite 80%. Unbounce's analysis of its landing-page data found video did not raise conversion rates on average.

claim: 93% of online experiences begin with a search engine
commonly_cited_as: "93% of online experiences begin with a search engine"
origin_publisher: Attributed to 'Forrester 2006' or imForza; no report found
origin_title: No study found
quote: A study by Forrester from 2006 found that 93% of all internet traffic comes from a search engine.
safe_rephrasing: Don't cite it; use current referral-traffic data with a named source.

claim: Americans check their phones 96 times a day
commonly_cited_as: "Americans check their phones 96 times a day" (as current)
origin_title: Americans Check Their Phones 96 Times a Day (press release)
quote: Asurion-sponsored survey by Market Research Firm Solidea Solutions conducted August 18-20, 2019 of 1,998 U.S. smartphone users
safe_rephrasing: In a 2019 Asurion-sponsored survey, US smartphone users reported checking their phones about 96 times a day.

claim: About 70% of online shopping carts are abandoned
commonly_cited_as: "The average cart abandonment rate is 70%"
origin_title: Cart Abandonment Rate Statistics (meta-average)
quote: we've calculated the average cart abandonment rate of 70.22 %. This value is an average calculated based on 50 different studies
safe_rephrasing: Baymard's average of 50 studies puts online cart abandonment at about 70%.

claim: The #1 Google result gets 31.7% of clicks
commonly_cited_as: "The top organic result gets 31.7% of clicks" (as current)
origin_title: Google CTR study (press release 27 Aug 2019)
quote: The #1 result in Google's search results receives 31.7% of all clicks
safe_rephrasing: A 2019 Backlinko/ClickFlow study of about 5 million results found the #1 organic result got 31.7% of clicks; newer studies report lower CTRs where AI Overviews appear.

claim: Influencer fraud costs brands $1.3 billion a year
commonly_cited_as: "Fake influencers cost brands $1.3 billion a year" (as measured)
origin_publisher: CHEQ with University of Baltimore economist Roberto Cavazos
origin_title: The Economic Cost of Bad Actors on the Internet: Fake Influencer Marketing
quote: fake influencer marketing will cost advertisers $1.3 billion in 2019
safe_rephrasing: A 2019 CHEQ-commissioned model estimated fake-influencer fraud at $1.3B, assuming 15% of $8.5B spend was lost.

claim: 80% of B2B leads from social media come from LinkedIn
commonly_cited_as: "80% of B2B social media leads come from LinkedIn" (as current)
origin_title: Analysis of 100,000+ posts (2014)
quote: Oktopost found that more than 80% of B2B leads were generated through LinkedIn.
safe_rephrasing: In 2014, Oktopost's analysis of its customers' posts attributed over 80% of their social B2B leads to LinkedIn.

claim: Only 3% of your market is ready to buy right now
commonly_cited_as: "Only 3% of buyers are actively buying" (the Buyer's Pyramid)
origin_title: Show-of-hands polls at live events
quote: Chet polled audiences by the thousands during his live events. He asked for a show of hands
safe_rephrasing: The '3% buying now' figure is a rule of thumb from informal seminar polls, not a measured market statistic.

claim: 90% of information transmitted to the brain is visual
commonly_cited_as: "90% of information transmitted to the brain is visual"
origin_title: No study cited
quote: the author simply states the 90% figure and doesn't indicate which study or research it came from.
safe_rephrasing: Don't cite it; no study supports a 90% figure.

claim: Users read only about 20% of the words on a web page
commonly_cited_as: "People only read 20% of the text on a page"
origin_title: How Little Do Users Read?
quote: On the average Web page, users have time to read at most 28% of the words during an average visit; 20% is more likely.
safe_rephrasing: NN/g estimated in 2008 that users have time to read at most 28% of a page's words, about 20% in practice.

claim: A 30-second Super Bowl ad costs about $8 million
commonly_cited_as: "A Super Bowl spot costs $8 million" (2026)
origin_publisher: NBCUniversal (as reported by Sports Business Journal)
origin_title: Super Bowl LX ad sales
quote: the average 30-second linear spot fetching an $8 million price.
safe_rephrasing: NBCUniversal's average price for a 30-second Super Bowl LX spot (2026) was about $8 million.

claim: Repeat customers spend 67% more than new customers
commonly_cited_as: "Bain: repeat customers spend 67% more than new ones"
origin_title: The Value of Online Customer Loyalty and How You Can Capture It
quote: In apparel, the average repeat customer spent 67 percent more in months 31-36 of his or her shopping relationship than in months zero-to-six.
safe_rephrasing: Bain's ~2000 study found online apparel customers spent 67% more in months 31-36 of the relationship than in their first six months.

claim: The influencer marketing industry is worth about $32.55 billion (2025)
commonly_cited_as: "Influencer marketing is a $32.55B industry"
origin_title: Influencer Marketing Statistics / Benchmark Report
quote: The global influencer marketing industry reached an estimated $32.55 billion in 2025
safe_rephrasing: Influencer Marketing Hub estimates the global influencer marketing industry at $32.55B in 2025.
